I1.quote: The isothermal ad/ab/desorption tests and TPD measurements are carried out in a Sievert-type pressure-composition-T apparatus (PCT, HPSA-auto device, China) ... −196/−186 °C isothermal volumetric H2 adsorption tests are done at liquid N2 and Ar, respectively.

I2.quote: Here, we prepared N-doped porous carbon (N-pC) from zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIF-8) by heat treatment. Its structure and composition are optimized by NH3 treatment to enrich N doping porous carbon (rN-pC)
I2.location: main, p. 5, Section 3.1 Preparation and Characterization of rN-pC

I3.quote: Excess gravimetric H2 uptake ~ 2.5 wt% at −196 °C and ~ 0.8 Mpa, and ~ 2.3 wt% at −186 °C and ~ 1.5 MPa is detected.
I3.location: main, p. 7, Section 3.2 Hydrogen Adsorption Properties of rN-pC (Fig. 2a)

I4.quote: BET tests give a 60MgH2@rN-pC SSA ~ 636.5 m2 g−1, much lower than pristine rN-pC (1525.4 m2 g−1).
I4.location: main, p. 9, Section 3.3 Preparation and Structural Characterization of 60MgH2@rN-pC

I5.quote: Nanoconfinement is a promising approach to simultaneously enhance the thermodynamics, kinetics, and cycling stability of hydrogen storage materials.

notes: I2 rests on the scaffold rN-pC measured on its own (Fig. 2a, Sieverts excess isotherms at -196 and -186 °C, 0-6 MPa); its XPS composition is C 91.48, N 5.97, O 2.55 at% (si1, p. 16, Table S2), so carbon is the majority by mass. The composite 60MgH2@rN-pC is ~60 wt% MgH2 (main, p. 3, Section 2.2.2), so it is not by itself a carbon sorbent; its -196 °C excess uptake (0.66 wt%, Fig. 4a) and the MgH2 absorption/desorption and TPD data do not decide eligibility. BET for rN-pC also in Table S1 (si1, p. 16): SBET 1525.4 m2 g-1. Text gives N-pC SSA 925.8 m2 g-1 (p. 5) while Table S1 gives 1146.5; irrelevant to eligibility. No retraction notice and no statement that the uptake data were published before.
